subject: Zenlea: request for extended audit log retention and supporting evidence
messages:
From: Evan Bates <evan.bates@zenlea.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Request: 180d audit log retention + evidence pack

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. Our security team (cc'd) is doing an updated SIG/CAIQ review ahead of our SOC 2 readiness and has asked whether Redwood can provide a customer-scoped exception to retain tenant audit and debug logs for 180 days instead of the default 30/90 windows for our account.

Specifically they are asking for: 
- written justification for the exception and any compensating controls;
- technical evidence of log storage location and retention enforcement (how deletion is scheduled/triggered);
- an example export manifest showing a search+export that would be provided on SAR/legal hold;
- confirmation of encryption at rest, key management, and proof of deletion for the standard 30d entries should we later request removal.

Is this something Redwood can support? If so, what's the shortest timeline to produce the evidence pack and a signed attestation? We prefer anything we can present to our auditors this month.

Appreciate it — Evan
Security Lead, Zenlea

On behalf of the Zenlea security team: security@zenlea.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Internal: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Evan Bates <evan.bates@zenlea.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: 180d audit log retention + evidence pack

Forwarding Zenlea's ask — they need a formal response and an evidence bundle (retention explanation, sample export manifest, encryption/KMS confirmation, and a deletion proof process).

Jonas — can you confirm the actual retention configuration for tenant-level audit logs and whether we can provision a customer-scoped exception (180d) as a: 
1) temporal policy change (T) we apply to the tenant metadata, and/or
2) a separate archival copy pinned to the customer's storage with access controls (A).

Please include the specific artifacts we can share (config snippets, example query + manifest, deletion workflow) and flag any risks or required approvals.

Marissa — we'll need compliance sign-off and an attestation draft if this is doable.

Ben — heads-up in case there are billing/contract implications for longer retention.

Thanks,
Hannah
Director, Customer Security Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Evan Bates <evan.bates@zenlea.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: 180d audit log retention + evidence pack

Hi team / Evan — quick rundown from infra: 

1) What we currently store: tenant-audit logs (auth events, API call metadata, admin actions) are written to the hot-store for 30 days, then moved to our cold-store tier (compressed) for an additional 60 days; debug-level ephemeral traces are purged after 7 days unless pinned by a support case.

2) Mechanism for extension: we can create a tenant-specific retention policy entry in the retention-service (policy_type: tenant_override) that sets audit log TTL = 180 days. Implementation is purely policy-level; logs remain in our managed object store under the same bucket naming convention (s3://redwood-logs/tenant/<tenant-id>/YYYY-MM-DD/). Deletion is driven by a scheduled job (retention-cleaner) which checks policy entries and removes objects older than TTL.

3) Compensating controls we recommend when increasing TTL: role-restricted access to archived buckets, separate KMS key for exported copies, and mandatory access logs for admin-side access. We can enable a narrow ACL that limits read to a Redwood Compliance IAM role and the customer's security principal (if they have a federation setup).

4) Evidence we can produce: 
- retention_policy_snippet.txt (contains the tenant_override JSON snippet with sanitized tenant-id);
- sample-logs-export-manifest.csv (example rows showing object keys, checksums, and timestamps);
- an activity log extract proving the retention-cleaner job runs (we can provide job-run entries for a date range);
- instructions & script to perform an ad-hoc export (we can run this and produce a tarball);
- description of the deletion proof process (object tombstones, versioning, and delete markers for S3-based store).

5) KMS/encryption: All objects at rest are encrypted with AES-256; we use a multi-tenant KMS key per region by default. For Zenlea we can create a customer-scoped CMK (customer-managed in our KMS) if requested; that will show up in the key policy and in our key-usage audit logs.

Risks / approvals: engineering can enable the tenant_override policy quickly (within 1 business day) but longer retention requires a compliance review for any business/legal constraints (we'll need Marissa to confirm). There may be a small recurring storage charge; Ben can advise.

I can attach the policy snippet and a sample manifest now. If Zenlea wants a signed attestation, Compliance can produce that once we agree to the terms.

-- Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: retention_policy_snippet.txt; sample-logs-export-manifest.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Evan Bates <evan.bates@zenlea.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: 180d audit log retention + evidence pack

Thanks Jonas — that matches what Compliance would expect. A few notes from our side before we provide anything outside the normal evidence set: 

- For SIG/CAIQ: provide the standard CAIQ mapping doc link plus the tenant_override policy snippet (sanitized). We should mark the exception as a "time-limited operational variance" and document compensating controls per SOC 2 AICPA guidance.

- Attestation: we can draft a one-page attestation letter describing the change (effective date, scope limited to audit logs, retention duration = 180 days) and the compensating controls (ACL, CMK, admin access logging). Compliance would require a sign-off from Legal on any contract addendum referencing data retention.

- Evidence proof-of-delete: we should produce both the export manifest and the retention-cleaner activity log extract. For the auditors, a screenshot of the S3 lifecycle rule & a job-run audit entry is often sufficient.

Next steps: 
1) Confirm Zenlea is OK with a time-limited exception (we usually propose a 12-month pilot review).
2) Jonas to produce sanitized artifacts (policy snippet, sample manifest, job-run entries).
3) Compliance (me) will prepare draft attestation_zenlea_180d_draft.pdf for internal review and then sent to Zenlea for signature.

I'll start the attestation draft today. Hannah, please confirm the pilot window and whether Zenlea needs a dedicated CMK.

Marissa
Principal Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Evan Bates <evan.bates@zenlea.com>, security@zenlea.com
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: 180d audit log retention + evidence pack

Hi Evan — quick update and proposal: 

1) We can enable a tenant-scoped retention override for Zenlea setting audit log TTL to 180 days. Jonas attached a sanitized policy snippet and a sample export manifest (see attachments). 

2) Compliance will issue a one-page attestation describing the exception and compensating controls; attached is the draft attestation_zenlea_180d_draft.pdf. We propose a 12-month pilot window (effective date upon signature) after which we will re-evaluate.

3) Artifacts we'll deliver within 3 business days after Zenlea confirms: 
   - retention_policy_snippet.txt (sanitized policy entry)
   - sample-logs-export-manifest.csv (example of object keys + checksums)
   - retention-cleaner audit entries for a recent week (to show deletion enforcement)
   - instructions & optional ad-hoc export tarball on request
   - signed attestation (once legal approvals are complete)

4) CMK option: we can provision a customer-managed CMK if you require it; this requires a short KMS onboarding form and may add ~2 business days.

Can you confirm: (A) acceptance of the 12-month pilot; (B) whether you want the CMK; (C) desired recipient for the signed attestation. Once confirmed we'll proceed and send the artifacts to your security mailbox.

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation so we can schedule delivery.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Security Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: retention_policy_snippet.txt; sample-logs-export-manifest.csv; attestation_zenlea_180d_draft.pdf
